entries.name: Avalonia
entries.use_for: Build native cross-platform desktop apps in C# and XAML.
entries.why: Leading cross-platform .NET UI framework (Windows, macOS, Linux), often used as a WPF successor.
entries.summary: Cross-platform .NET UI framework using XAML with a flexible styling system, targeting Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android and WebAssembly. Often seen as a spiritual successor to WPF and used by JetBrains, Unity and others.
entries.best_for: C#/.NET desktop apps that must run on Windows, macOS and Linux with a WPF-like experience.
entries.not_for: Native platform controls (it draws its own UI) or non-.NET stacks; not a 1:1 WPF copy.

entries.name: ClawX
entries.use_for: Give OpenClaw AI agents a desktop GUI with setup wizard, chat, provider settings and skill management.
entries.why: Embeds the OpenClaw runtime, so there is no separate install and no terminal needed.
entries.summary: A desktop app built on the official OpenClaw core. It replaces CLI setup with a guided wizard, visual settings, a chat interface and automatic Gateway lifecycle management. It supports Windows and several languages.
entries.best_for: Using OpenClaw agents without the command line, or forking a desktop shell for an agent runtime.
entries.not_for: Tied to OpenClaw. It is an end-user app, not a library for building your own agents.

entries.name: DeckCraft
entries.use_for: Open, edit and present PowerPoint files in a native Rust app that agents can also drive.
entries.why: Every UI action is also a command for the CLI and for AI agents through MCP.
entries.summary: A clean-room Rust reimplementation of a slide editor with themes, shapes, tables, charts, transitions and animations. It opens and saves PowerPoint files, runs on macOS, Windows, Linux and in the browser, and exposes a CLI and MCP.
entries.best_for: Rust developers who want an open slide editor or a scriptable way to build and render decks.
entries.not_for: The README says it is in alpha, heading for beta. Expect gaps against PowerPoint.

entries.name: DesignCraft
entries.use_for: Use or fork an open page-layout editor with IDML import and PDF/X export.
entries.why: Clean-room Rust layout app with a Knuth-Plass composer and an MCP server.
entries.summary: A native and WebAssembly page-layout editor modeled on InDesign workflows. It has threaded frames, styles, parent pages, IDML and INDD import, PDF, EPUB and PNG export, a headless CLI, and a JSON control channel and MCP server.
entries.best_for: Building publishing tools or scripting page layout from agents and the command line.
entries.not_for: A large app with an egui frontend that needs a recent Rust toolchain. Not a drop-in for all InDesign files.

entries.name: Deta Surf
entries.use_for: Fork or study a local-first AI notebook that organizes files and web pages and writes notes from them.
entries.why: Stores data locally in open formats and lets you choose any model, including local ones.
entries.summary: A desktop AI notebook built with Svelte, TypeScript and Rust for macOS, Windows and Linux. It keeps a local library of files and web content, generates notes with citations linked to sources, and can make small interactive apps.
entries.best_for: Researchers who want a local AI notebook, or developers who want a base for a similar app.
entries.not_for: A finished end-user app rather than a library. The excerpt does not say if development is active.

entries.name: Eclipse Theia
entries.use_for: Framework for building custom desktop and cloud IDEs and tools
entries.why: Eclipse-governed IDE platform supporting VS Code extensions; basis for products like Arduino IDE 2; EPL-2.0.
entries.summary: Extensible framework for building multi-language cloud and desktop IDEs and tools with web technologies; supports VS Code extensions and is the basis for products like Arduino IDE 2. EPL-2.0.
entries.best_for: Building a custom IDE or tool platform with VS Code extension compatibility.
entries.not_for: Ordinary desktop apps or simple editors; large framework with significant customization effort.

entries.name: egui
entries.use_for: Easy immediate-mode GUI for Rust that runs natively and on the web
entries.why: The most popular Rust GUI library; fast to build tools and runs on desktop and WASM
entries.summary: Immediate-mode GUI library for Rust that runs natively, on the web (WASM) and in game engines. eframe is the official framework for Web, Linux, Mac, Windows and Android.
entries.best_for: Quick tools, debug UIs and apps in Rust, including web demos via WASM.
entries.not_for: Apps needing native look and feel, rich accessibility, or complex retained-mode layouts.

entries.name: Electron
entries.use_for: Build cross-platform desktop apps with HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
entries.why: Powers VS Code, Slack and Discord; the most mature web-tech desktop framework with a huge ecosystem.
entries.summary: Framework for cross-platform desktop apps with JavaScript, HTML and CSS, bundling Node.js and Chromium. Powers apps like VS Code.
entries.best_for: Desktop apps with web tech, fullest ecosystem and consistent rendering across OSes.
entries.not_for: Small, memory-light binaries (bundles Chromium, so apps are large). Consider Tauri or Neutralino.

entries.name: Electron Forge
entries.use_for: Official all-in-one tool to scaffold, package, sign and publish Electron apps
entries.why: The Electron team's recommended build pipeline with Vite/Webpack templates and makers for every OS
entries.summary: Electron Forge is a tool for building Electron applications that unifies existing Electron build tools into one package. You scaffold a project with npx create-electron-app, and it handles build tooling, native module rebuilding (via @electron/rebuild) and packaging for release.
entries.best_for: Starting or packaging an Electron desktop app with one standard toolchain from scaffolding to distributable.
entries.not_for: Electron only; not for Tauri or other desktop frameworks. Requires Node 22.17.0 or higher and Git.

entries.name: electron-builder
entries.use_for: Package, sign and publish Electron apps as installers with auto-update support.
entries.why: The standard Electron packaging tool: DMG, NSIS, AppImage, Snap and more, plus code signing and electron-updater.
entries.summary: Packaging and build tool for Electron apps producing installers for macOS, Windows and Linux (DMG, NSIS, AppImage, Snap and more), with code signing, publishing and electron-updater auto-update support.
entries.best_for: Distributing Electron apps with polished installers and auto-updates.
entries.not_for: Non-Electron frameworks; heavy configuration for simple cases, and Forge is the official alternative.

entries.name: electron-vite
entries.use_for: Vite-based build tooling for Electron main, preload and renderer processes
entries.why: Fast HMR-based dev setup for Electron with sensible defaults; widely used for modern Electron apps
entries.summary: Vite-based build tooling for Electron main, preload and renderer processes with sensible defaults, fast HMR, isolated multi-entry builds, optional V8 bytecode source protection and support for TypeScript, Vue, React, Svelte and Solid.
entries.best_for: Modern Electron dev setup with fast hot reload and Vite-style configuration.
entries.not_for: Non-Electron projects; handles building, not packaging or installers.

entries.name: Flet
entries.use_for: Build desktop, web and mobile apps in Python with Flutter-rendered UI
entries.why: Easiest way to ship cross-platform GUIs from Python without frontend experience
entries.summary: Python framework for building web, desktop and mobile apps without frontend experience; the UI renders with Flutter and apps are written as Python code. Flet Studio offers an online playground.
entries.best_for: Python developers wanting cross-platform GUIs quickly without HTML/JS.
entries.not_for: Highly custom native UI or large apps needing the full Flutter/Dart ecosystem; runtime size is larger.

entries.name: Fyne
entries.use_for: Cross-platform GUI toolkit for Go: desktop and mobile from one codebase
entries.why: The most popular Go GUI toolkit; material-style widgets and simple packaging
entries.summary: Easy-to-use UI toolkit and app API in Go for desktop and mobile from a single codebase. Requires Go 1.22+ and a C compiler.
entries.best_for: Go apps needing simple, portable GUIs on desktop and mobile.
entries.not_for: Native look and feel or complex rich UIs; needs a C toolchain.

entries.name: iced
entries.use_for: Cross-platform Elm-inspired GUI library for Rust
entries.why: Leading Rust native GUI toolkit; used by System76's COSMIC desktop
entries.summary: Cross-platform GUI library for Rust inspired by Elm, with a type-safe reactive model, built-in widgets, responsive layout, async support and time-travel debugging. Targets Windows, macOS, Linux and web.
entries.best_for: Rust desktop apps using Elm-style architecture; used by System76's COSMIC desktop.
entries.not_for: Mature accessibility and rich widgets out of the box, or quick prototypes; API still evolving.

entries.name: Native SDK
entries.use_for: Build native desktop apps from TypeScript logic and Native markup, compiled to a native executable.
entries.why: Compiles app logic and views to a native binary and renders in OS windows, with live reload while developing.
entries.summary: A toolkit that compiles TypeScript app logic and Native markup into a native executable. The native CLI covers init, dev, check and build. Zig cores and optional embedded web content are also supported.
entries.best_for: Developers who know TypeScript and want a native desktop app instead of an Electron-style web shell.
entries.not_for: The README calls it experimental. Platform support varies and mobile is still evolving. Needs Node.js 24 or later and a Zig toolchain.

entries.name: Netcatty
entries.use_for: Manage SSH, SFTP and terminal sessions in one workspace, or fork a modern SSH client.
entries.why: Combines split terminals, a dual-pane SFTP browser and a built-in AI agent in one Electron app.
entries.summary: An SSH client and terminal manager for macOS, Windows and Linux built with Electron, React and xterm.js. It supports SSH, Telnet, Mosh, serial and local terminals, with tabs, split panes, vault views and SFTP.
entries.best_for: Developers and sysadmins who want a PuTTY or Termius alternative they can read and modify.
entries.not_for: Use inside proprietary products: it is GPL-3.0. It is an end-user app, not a library, and not a shell replacement.

entries.name: Neutralinojs
entries.use_for: Lightweight cross-platform desktop apps with JS, HTML and CSS using the system webview
entries.why: Tiny binaries without bundling Chromium or Node; language-agnostic extensions

license_verified.note: Core MIT; bundled third-party libraries keep their own permissive licenses

entries.summary: Lightweight desktop app framework using HTML, CSS and JavaScript on the system webview, without bundling Chromium or Node. Runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, Web and Chrome, extensible via IPC extensions in any language; neu CLI.
entries.best_for: Tiny portable desktop apps in web tech without Electron overhead.
entries.not_for: Apps needing Node.js APIs or consistent Chromium rendering; smaller ecosystem.

entries.name: NW.js
entries.use_for: Build desktop apps with HTML, CSS and JS with Node.js APIs available in the DOM
entries.why: Long-standing Electron alternative with direct Node access from web pages and source protection
entries.summary: App runtime based on Chromium and Node.js that lets you build native apps in HTML and JavaScript and call Node.js modules directly from the DOM. Originally node-webkit, created at Intel.
entries.best_for: Desktop apps wanting direct Node access in web pages and source protection.
entries.not_for: Teams wanting the larger Electron ecosystem or small binaries; bundles Chromium.

entries.name: OpenLess
entries.use_for: Hold a hotkey, speak, and get AI-polished text inserted at your cursor in any app.
entries.why: Open source alternative to Wispr Flow-style tools, with custom style packs and a prompt-writing mode.
entries.summary: OpenLess is a voice input app for macOS, Windows and Linux. You press a global hotkey and speak; it transcribes, polishes the text in a chosen style, and inserts it at the cursor, or copies it if insertion is blocked. It has an AI-prompt mode, a learning dictionary, optional cursor context, and shareable style packs.
entries.best_for: You want a hackable dictation tool, or a base to fork for your own voice input app.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0, so modified network use must share source. Needs speech and polish models through its own settings. A finished desktop app, not an SDK.

entries.name: Pake
entries.use_for: Wrap an existing website into a lightweight desktop app with one command.
entries.why: Tauri-based CLI that produces small native apps (~5 MB) from a URL; far lighter than Electron wrappers.
entries.summary: Tauri-based CLI that turns any website into a lightweight desktop app with one command for macOS, Windows and Linux; installers are typically under 10MB with shortcuts and style customization.
entries.best_for: Wrapping an existing website or web app into a small desktop app quickly.
entries.not_for: Apps needing custom native logic or offline-first local code; it is a wrapper around a URL.

entries.name: PakePlus
entries.use_for: Package any webpage or web app into a small desktop/mobile app
entries.why: Tauri-based wrapper producing ~5MB apps from a URL or HTML build, with GUI and CI builds; MIT.
entries.summary: Tauri-based tool packaging any webpage or web app into small desktop and mobile apps (about 5MB) from a URL or HTML build, with a GUI and CI builds. MIT; the README says front-end code is no longer open source.
entries.best_for: Quickly packaging a webpage or built frontend as a desktop or mobile app without a local toolchain.
entries.not_for: Users requiring fully open-source code (README says front-end closed) or deep native customization.

entries.name: pywebview
entries.use_for: Lightweight wrapper to show HTML UIs in a native webview window from Python
entries.why: The go-to way to build web-UI desktop apps in Python with a JS-Python bridge
entries.summary: Lightweight Python wrapper that shows HTML in a native GUI window using WinForms, Cocoa, or Qt/GTK webviews. Includes a built-in HTTP server, DOM support in Python, window management and a JS-Python bridge.
entries.best_for: Python desktop apps with web UIs, without bundling a heavy toolkit.
entries.not_for: Apps needing native widgets or consistent engines across platforms (uses system webviews).

entries.name: SideX
entries.use_for: Running a lighter-weight VS Code workbench without Electron's memory overhead, with a built-in bring-your-own-model AI agent.
entries.why: Targets under 200 MB at idle on macOS by using the OS's native webview instead of bundled Chromium.
entries.summary: SideX ports the VS Code TypeScript workbench, editor, terminal and Git integration onto a Rust/Tauri backend instead of Electron. Core editing, terminal and Git are solid; the extension host and debugger are still in progress, and it ships a built-in AI agent that needs no account or sign-in.
entries.best_for: Developers wanting VS Code's familiar editing experience with lower memory use, especially on macOS.
entries.not_for: Not ready if you depend heavily on extensions or the debugger, since the extension host and debugger are still in progress.

entries.name: Slint
entries.use_for: Declarative UI toolkit for native desktop, embedded and mobile apps from Rust, C++, JS or Python
entries.why: Native UI with its own markup language; GPL-3.0, royalty-free and commercial options

license_verified.note: Triple-licensed: GPL-3.0-only, Slint Royalty-free 2.0 (proprietary desktop/mobile/web, not embedded) or commercial

entries.summary: Declarative UI toolkit for native desktop, embedded and mobile apps: define UI in .slint markup and connect to logic in Rust, C++, JavaScript or Python. Scalable and lightweight. GPL-3.0 with royalty-free and commercial options.
entries.best_for: Native UIs for embedded devices and desktop with low resource use.
entries.not_for: Proprietary projects wanting no license obligations (check GPL/royalty-free terms) or web-centric stacks.

entries.name: SuperCmd
entries.use_for: Use or fork an open-source macOS launcher that runs Raycast extensions and adds AI, dictation and read-aloud.
entries.why: Includes a @raycast/api and @raycast/utils compatibility layer, so existing Raycast extensions work.
entries.summary: An Electron and React launcher for macOS with native Swift and Objective-C parts. It offers AI chat, hold-to-speak dictation, text-to-speech, clipboard history, snippets, notes, a canvas, file search and window tiling.
entries.best_for: Raycast-style workflows on an open-source base, or a reference for Raycast API compatibility.
entries.not_for: macOS only. A user app more than a library, and compatibility with the Raycast API is a shim, not a guarantee for every extension.

entries.name: Tauri
entries.use_for: Build small, secure desktop (and mobile) apps with a web frontend and a Rust backend.
entries.why: Uses the OS webview instead of bundling Chromium, so binaries are a few MB; strong security model and plugin system.
entries.summary: Framework for small, secure desktop and mobile apps with any web frontend and a Rust backend. Uses the OS webview via WRY and tao rather than bundling Chromium, with a plugin system and security model.
entries.best_for: Lightweight cross-platform apps with a web UI and Rust-side native capabilities.
entries.not_for: Needing identical Chromium rendering everywhere or avoiding Rust; system webview differences apply.

entries.name: Terax
entries.use_for: Use or fork a small terminal-first AI dev environment with editor, git and web preview built in.
entries.why: About 7 to 8 MB, no telemetry or account, and works with your own keys or local models.
entries.summary: A Tauri 2 and Rust desktop app with a GPU terminal, an agentic AI side panel, a CodeMirror editor with inline AI diffs, file explorer, source control with a git graph, and a web preview pane. It runs with your own keys or fully local models.
entries.best_for: Developers who want a light, private alternative to heavier AI IDEs.
entries.not_for: Stable dependency use. The README says a major v0.9.0 rewrite is in progress, including a switch from xterm.js to libghostty.

entries.name: Wails
entries.use_for: Build desktop apps with a Go backend and any web frontend.
entries.why: Go equivalent of Tauri: native webview, generated TS bindings to Go methods and small binaries.
entries.summary: Builds desktop apps with a Go backend and any web frontend, bundled into a single binary using the native webview. Provides project creation, compilation and bundling tools plus bindings from Go methods.
entries.best_for: Go developers wanting desktop apps with web UIs and small binaries.
entries.not_for: Non-Go backends or Chromium-consistent rendering; relies on system webview.

entries.name: ZTools
entries.use_for: Run or extend an application launcher with plugins, clipboard history and pinyin search.
entries.why: Open source take on uTools with UI and headless plugins, LMDB storage and native clipboard and window modules.
entries.summary: ZTools is an application launcher and plugin platform for macOS and Windows. It offers quick launch with pinyin and regex search, clipboard history, themes, isolated plugin data, a plugin market and TypeScript types for plugin authors. Built with Electron, Vue 3, LMDB and C++ native modules.
entries.best_for: You want a hackable launcher you can write plugins for, or a base to fork.
entries.not_for: Desktop only (macOS and Windows), no Linux. It is an independent reimplementation of uTools, so plugin compatibility is not promised in the README.
